item.title: Lighting, signs and fire preventative measures, 19th August
item.description:
I am writing to urgently request that further fire safety measures be implemented in the park area adjacent to my property. There have been several recent incidents that have left me deeply concerned for the safety of my home, my wellbeing, and the wider community. I On the night of August 5th at 11:55pm, I awoke to a fire in the park behind a neighbour’s garden. I called the fire brigade who struggled to get their hoses to this area as the access point are overgrown and not visable. the other access point noone can get though and maybe their need to be access closer to the jolly farmers roundabuts. A few days later I witnessed three young men throwing items into the bushes and graffitiing the bins and bench at approx 12pm at night. Then a couple nights later, a young girl was seen smoking on the bench at 10pm at night. On August 18th, I had to call the fire brigade again due to another fire in the bushes near my property. These repeated incidents are causing me severe anxiety and panic attacks, especially as I have previously lost my home to fire. I am exhausted and struggling to cope with the ongoing risk and disruption to my life. I also have asthma and need to sleep with my window open. The persistent smoke and fumes from these fires are making my symptoms significantly worse. The thing waking me up is that I can hear the fires crackling at night, which often sounds like rain, making me keep checking outside constantly. I feel I am the only one waking up to these incidents, which means I have to stay alert at night, further impacting my sleep and wellbeing. While I appreciate that the grass is cut regularly, which I hope helps create a fire break, it is clear that more needs to be done to prevent further incidents. Based on guidance from Bexley Council’s own procedures and the London Fire Brigade, I am requesting the following additional measures: * Installation of improved lighting in the park to deter unlawful behaviour at night * Erection of clear signage warning against starting fires, smoking, and illegal dumping * Placement of more bins and dedicated smoking disposal units to reduce litter and fire hazards * Removal of the bench, as it has become a focal point for anti-social behaviour and is not otherwise used by the community * Increased monitoring and collaboration with Environmental Health and the local fire brigade for recurring incidents I have reported these incidents and documented dates, times, and observations, as advised. However, I am not sure what else I can do on my own. I urge you to take these concerns seriously and to put in place the recommended fire safety and preventative measures as soon as possible, in line with council policy and best practice. Thank you for your attention and support in helping to keep our community safe.
